The net is a sagging blue hammock strung between vertical silver metal posts over the pool water. The boy is now sitting in the hollow of the top of the net, barefoot, with both soles resting on the blue ropes themselves. He is dry, unlike the children in the water below him.

The left-hand end of that net is anchored at the dark brown paved pool deck. Other barefoot, dry boys are standing on that deck at the edge of the pool beside the posts, at the entry to the net. That deck is the only broad, foot-sized, dry solid surface adjacent to the net from which he could have entered.

He did not climb from the water, because he is dry. He did not climb from the top of a silver post, because those posts are narrow vertical cylinders with rounded caps, taller than the net attachment, with no platform for feet, and he is positioned in the middle of the sag between posts, not above a post. He did not climb from the scissor-lift or another person.

He therefore walked barefoot across the poolside deck paving to the end of the net and then stepped or crawled out onto the ropes and up onto the top where he is now sitting. The last non-rope surface his feet touched before climbing onto the top of the ropes was the pool-deck pavement.

criteria.justification: The candidate states the boy 'most likely last had his feet on the poolside deck paving' before climbing onto the ropes.
